q: सेल्यूकस निकेटर द्वारा पाटलिपुत्र में चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के दरबार में भेजा गया वह यूनानी राजदूत कौन था जिसने "इंडिका" की रचना की?
e: Megasthenes resided at Chandragupta Maurya's court (c. 302–298 BCE) and wrote "Indica" (preserved via fragments in Strabo, Arrian, Diodorus), describing Pataliputra's 6 municipal boards of 5 members each and dividing Indian society into 7 classes. Exam Boosters: (1) Deimachus visited Bindusara's court (sent by Antiochus I of Syria); Dionysius visited Bindusara/Ashoka (sent by Ptolemy II Philadelphus of Egypt). (2) Greek writers called Chandragupta "Sandrocottus" (identified by Sir William Jones in 1793).
qe: Who was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra, who authored "Indica"?

q: अपने अंतिम वर्षों में चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य ने भद्रबाहु के मार्गदर्शन में जैन धर्म अपनाया और किस स्थान पर संलेखना (उपवास द्वारा देहत्याग) विधि से प्राण त्यागे?
e: Chandragupta Maurya migrated to Chandragiri Hill at Shravanabelagola (Hassan district, Karnataka) with Jain Acharya Bhadrabahu and performed Sallekhana (c. 297 BCE). Exam Boosters: (1) His son Bindusara was known to Greeks as "Amitrochates" (Sanskrit: Amitraghata — Slayer of Foes) and patronized the Ajivika sect.
qe: In his later years, Chandragupta Maurya embraced Jainism under the guidance of Bhadrabahu and ended his life through the Jain ritual of Sallekhana (fasting unto death) at:

q: किस मौर्य शासक ने अपने शासनकाल के 14वें वर्ष में (वृहत् शिलालेख V में उल्लिखित) नैतिक कल्याण के प्रचार हेतु "धम्म महामात्र" नामक विशेष अधिकारियों की नियुक्ति की थी?
e: Emperor Ashoka appointed Dhamma Mahamattas in his 13th/14th regnal year (Major Rock Edict V) to promote Dhamma (non-violence, religious tolerance, respect for elders/servants) across all sects and frontier regions. Exam Boosters: (1) Ashoka's Dhamma was an ethical code of conduct, NOT a sectarian religion (defined in Pillar Edicts II & VII). (2) Brihadratha was the last Mauryan ruler, assassinated by Pushyamitra Shunga in 185 BCE.
qe: Which Mauryan ruler appointed special officers called "Dhamma Mahamattas" (धम्म महामात्र) in the 14th year of his reign (mentioned in Major Rock Edict V) to propagate moral welfare?

q: कौन-सा अशोक अभिलेख पुष्टि करता है कि गौतम बुद्ध का जन्म लुम्बिनी (रुम्मिनदेई) में हुआ था तथा अशोक ने वहाँ का भू-राजस्व (भाग) घटाकर 1/8 कर दिया और 'बलि' कर माफ कर दिया?
e: The Rummindei (Lumbini, Nepal) Pillar Inscription—dated to Ashoka's 20th regnal year—is the most important economic inscription of Ashoka ("Hida Budhe Jate Sakyamuniti"). Exam Boosters: (1) Bhabru (Bairat, Rajasthan) Edict expresses Ashoka's explicit faith in the Buddhist Triratna (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha) and calls him "Piyadassi Laja Magadhe". (2) Allahabad Pillar carries the Queen's Edict (Karuvaki) as well as Samudragupta's Prayag Prashasti.
qe: Which Ashokan inscription confirms that Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini (Rummindei) and records Ashoka reducing the village's land revenue (Bhaga) to 1/8th and exempting it from Bali?

q:
सूची-I (कौटिल्य के अर्थशास्त्र में मौर्य अधिकारी) को सूची-II (विभाग / कार्य) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. समाहर्ता — (a) राजकीय कोषाध्यक्ष
2. सन्निधाता — (b) राजस्व संग्रहकर्ता महाधिकारी
3. सीताध्यक्ष — (c) राजकीय कृषि विभाग का अध्यक्ष
4. पण्याध्यक्ष — (d) वाणिज्य एवं व्यापार का अध्यक्ष
e: Samaharta was the Chief Revenue Collector (1-b); Sannidhata was the Chief Treasurer/Keeper of Royal Granaries (2-a); Sitadhyaksha managed state-owned agricultural lands called 'Sita' (3-c); and Panyadhyaksha regulated trade and market prices (4-d). Exam Boosters: (1) Arthashastra (15 Adhikaranas/books, discovered by R. Shamasastry in 1905) lists 18 Tirthas (high officials) and 27 Adhyakshas (superintendents).
qe:
Match List-I (Mauryan Official in Kautilya's Arthashastra) with List-II (Department / Duty):
1. Samaharta (समाहर्ता) — (a) Chief Treasurer / Custodian of Treasury
2. Sannidhata (सन्निधाता) — (b) Collector-General of Revenue
3. Sitadhyaksha (सीताध्यक्ष) — (c) Superintendent of Crown Agriculture
4. Panyadhyaksha (पण्याध्यक्ष) — (d) Superintendent of Commerce & Trade

q: कौटिल्य के अर्थशास्त्र में मौर्यकाल के दो प्रकार के न्यायालय कौन-से थे?
e: Mauryan judiciary had two distinct courts: Dharmasthiya (धर्मस्थीय — Civil courts dealing with marriage, inheritance, property, contracts) and Kantakashodhana (कंटकशोधन — Criminal courts literally meaning "removal of thorns", headed by Pradeshtas).
qe: In Kautilya's Arthashastra, the two types of law courts during the Mauryan period were:

q: पश्चिमोत्तर सीमांत क्षेत्र (वर्तमान पाकिस्तान में शाहबाजगढ़ी और मानसेहरा) से प्राप्त अशोक के अभिलेखों में किस लिपि का प्रयोग हुआ है?
e: While most Ashokan inscriptions across India are in Prakrit language and Brahmi script, the Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra rock edicts are in Kharosthi script (written right-to-left). Exam Boosters: (1) The Kandahar (Shar-i-Kuna, Afghanistan) edict is bilingual in Greek and Aramaic scripts. (2) Taxila and Laghman edicts are in Aramaic script.
qe: Which scripts were used in Ashoka's inscriptions discovered in the north-western frontier region (Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra in present-day Pakistan)?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा मौर्य प्रांत और उसकी राजधानी सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e: The capital of Kalinga province (conquered by Ashoka in 261 BCE) was Tosali (Dhauli, Odisha), NOT Kausambi. The 5th province was Prachyapatha / Magadha with capital Pataliputra.
qe: Which of the following Mauryan provinces and their capitals is NOT correctly matched?

q: सारनाथ के प्रसिद्ध एकाश्म पॉलिशदार बलुआ पत्थर के सिंह-शीर्ष (26 जनवरी 1950 को भारत का राष्ट्रीय प्रतीक अपनाया गया) की चौकी (abacus) पर कौन-से चार पशु उत्कीर्ण हैं?
e: The abacus of the Sarnath Lion Capital depicts four galloping animals separated by 24-spoked wheels (Dharmachakras): Elephant (East), Bull (West), Horse (South), and Lion (North). Exam Boosters: (1) The Barabar Caves (Bihar—Lomas Rishi, Sudama, Karna Chaupar, Vishva Zopri) were excavated by Ashoka for the Ajivika sect (and Nagarjuni Caves by his grandson Dasharatha).
qe: The famous monolithic polished sandstone Lion Capital at Sarnath (adopted as India's National Emblem on 26 January 1950) features four animals carved on its abacus. Which four animals are they?

q: अशोक का कौन-सा वृहत् शिलालेख स्पष्ट रूप से सभी संप्रदायों के प्रति धार्मिक सहिष्णुता व सद्भाव ("अपने संप्रदाय का सम्मान करते हुए दूसरे की निंदा न करना") का उपदेश देता है?
e: Major Rock Edict VII and especially Major Rock Edict XII are celebrated charters of religious tolerance (सहिष्णुता). Exam Boosters: (1) Rock Edict I prohibits animal sacrifice in festive gatherings (Samaja). (2) Rock Edict II mentions medical care for humans/animals and southern neighbours (Cholas, Pandyas, Satyaputras, Keralaputras, Tamraparni).
qe: Which Ashokan Major Rock Edict explicitly advocates religious tolerance and harmony among all sects ("one should not honour one's own sect while disparaging another's")?

q: कौटिल्य के राज्य के "सप्तांग सिद्धांत" में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा राज्य के सात अंगों में सम्मिलित नहीं है?
e: Kautilya's 7 limbs (Prakritis) of the state are: Swami (King), Amatya (Ministers), Janapada (Territory/Population), Durga (Fort), Kosha (Treasury), Danda/Bala (Army/Force), and Mitra (Ally). Purohita and Sangha are not among the seven limbs.
qe: In Kautilya's Saptanga Theory (सप्तांग सिद्धांत) of the State, which of the following is NOT one of the seven limbs (constituent elements) of the state?

q: कौन-सा मौर्य अभिलेख राजकीय अकाल राहत उपायों (आपातकाल में वितरण हेतु राजकीय कोष्ठागारों में अनाज भंडारण) का प्राचीनतम पुरातात्विक प्रमाण देता है?
e: The Sohgaura Copper Plate (Gorakhpur, UP) and Mahasthan Stone Plaque (Bogra, Bangladesh)—both in Mauryan Brahmi—record orders for storing grain in royal granaries (Koshthagara) for distribution during famine.
qe: Which Mauryan inscription provides the earliest archaeological evidence of state famine relief measures (storing grain in royal granaries to distribute during distress)?

q:
मौर्यकालीन समाज एवं अर्थव्यवस्था के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: मेगस्थनीज ने कहा कि भारत में दास प्रथा नहीं थी, जबकि कौटिल्य के अर्थशास्त्र में कानूनी अधिकारों सहित दासों की नौ श्रेणियों का स्पष्ट उल्लेख है।
कथन II: चाँदी का आहत सिक्का "पण" (Pana) मौर्य साम्राज्य की मानक मुद्रा थी।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: न तो I और न ही II
e: Both statements are correct. Megasthenes missed Indian slavery because Indian slaves (Dasas) were treated far more humanely than Greek slaves and could earn their freedom (as detailed in Arthashastra). The silver Pana (Karshapana) was the standard Mauryan coin (peacock/hill/crescent symbols).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Mauryan society and economy:
Statement I: Megasthenes stated that there was no slavery in India, whereas Kautilya's Arthashastra explicitly lists nine categories of slaves (Dasas) with legal rights.
Statement II: The silver punch-marked coin called "Pana" (पण) was the standard currency of the Mauryan Empire.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: अर्थशास्त्र में वर्णित मौर्य गुप्तचर व्यवस्था में एक स्थान पर स्थायी रूप से रहने वाले गुप्तचर "संस्था" कहलाते थे, जबकि राज्य में भ्रमण करने वाले गुप्तचर क्या कहलाते थे?
e: Kautilya divided spies (collectively called Gudhapurusha) into two categories: Samstha (संस्था — stationary spies) and Sanchara (संचरा — roving/wandering spies, including women spies).
qe: In the Mauryan espionage system described in the Arthashastra, spies stationed permanently at one place were called "Samstha", whereas wandering spies who travelled across the kingdom were called:

q: 185 ई.पू. में अंतिम मौर्य शासक बृहद्रथ की हत्या करके शुंग वंश की स्थापना किसने की और पतंजलि के पौरोहित्य में दो अश्वमेध यज्ञ कराए?
e: Pushyamitra Shunga (commander-in-chief of Brihadratha) founded the Shunga dynasty (185–73 BCE). His two Ashvamedha sacrifices are corroborated by the Ayodhya Inscription of Dhanadeva and Patanjali's Mahabhashya. Exam Boosters: (1) His son Agnimitra is the hero of Kalidasa's play "Malavikagnimitram". (2) Bharhut Stupa and the stone railings/toranas of Sanchi Stupa were built during the Shunga period.
qe: Who founded the Shunga Dynasty in 185 BCE after assassinating the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha, and performed two Ashvamedha sacrifices (with Patanjali as priest)?

q: 78 ई. में प्रारंभ होने वाला "शक संवत्" (जिसे 1957 में भारत के राष्ट्रीय पंचांग के रूप में अपनाया गया) परंपरागत रूप से किस कुषाण सम्राट के राज्यारोहण से संबद्ध है?
e: Kanishka I (most famous Kushana ruler, capitals Purushapura/Peshawar and Mathura) initiated the Shaka Era in 78 CE. Exam Boosters: (1) Vima Kadphises was the first Kushana ruler to issue extensive gold coins in India (bearing Shiva, Nandi, and Trishula). (2) Kanishka's Rabatak Inscription (Afghanistan) details the Kushana genealogy and empire extent.
qe: The Shaka Era (शक संवत्), which begins in 78 CE and was adopted as India's official national calendar in 1957, is traditionally associated with the accession of which Kushana emperor?

q: दक्कन के किस राजवंश ने भारतीय इतिहास में सर्वप्रथम ब्राह्मणों एवं बौद्ध भिक्षुओं को कर-मुक्त भूमि अनुदान (अग्रहार) देने की प्रथा शुरू की और मुख्यतः सीसे (Lead) के सिक्के चलाए?
e: The Satavahanas (founded by Simuka, capital Pratishthana/Paithan; called Andhras in Puranas) initiated land grants (recorded in Naneghat & Nasik inscriptions) and issued lead, potin, copper, and silver coins. Exam Boosters: (1) Gautamiputra Satakarni (c. 106–130 CE, praised in Nasik Prashasti by his mother Gautami Balashri as "Ekabrahmana" and destroyer of Shaka king Nahapana) was the greatest Satavahana king. (2) King Hala compiled the Prakrit anthology "Gatha Saptashati".
qe: Which dynasty in the Deccan was the FIRST in Indian history to grant tax-free land (Agrahara / Brahmadeya) to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks, and predominantly issued coins made of LEAD (सीसा)?

q: 150 ई. का जूनागढ़ (गिरनार) शिलालेख—शुद्ध क्लासिकी संस्कृत में लिखा गया प्राचीनतम विस्तृत अभिलेख—किस शक पश्चिमी क्षत्रप शासक ने सुदर्शन झील की मरम्मत के उल्लेख हेतु जारी किया था?
e: Shaka Kardamaka ruler Rudradaman I (130–150 CE) issued the Junagadh inscription in pure Sanskrit prose, recording that he repaired the embankment of Sudarshana Lake (originally built by Pushyagupta under Chandragupta Maurya and equipped with canals by Tushaspha under Ashoka) from his own treasury without imposing forced labour (Vishti).
qe: The Junagadh (Girnar) Rock Inscription of 150 CE—the earliest long inscription in chaste classical Sanskrit—was issued by which Shaka Western Kshatrapa ruler to record the repair of Sudarshana Lake?

q: सम्राट कनिष्क के दरबार के विद्वानों और उनकी प्रसिद्ध रचनाओं के निम्नलिखित युग्मों में से कौन-सा सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e: Patanjali (author of Mahabhashya) was a contemporary of Pushyamitra Shunga (2nd century BCE), NOT Kanishka (1st–2nd century CE). Ashvaghosha (Buddhacharita, Saundarananda, Sariputraprakarana), Charaka (royal physician), Vasumitra, and Nagarjuna were associated with Kanishka's court.
qe: Which of the following pairs of scholars at Emperor Kanishka's court and their famous works is NOT correctly matched?

q: कुषाण काल के दौरान निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी विशेषता "गांधार कला शैली" को "मथुरा कला शैली" से अलग करती है?
o: गांधार में भूरे-नीले शिस्ट पत्थर व यूनानी-रोमन यथार्थवाद का प्रयोग हुआ, जबकि मथुरा में चित्तीदार लाल बलुआ पत्थर व स्वदेशी आध्यात्मिक शैली का
गांधार में तीनों धर्मों की मूर्तियाँ बनीं, जबकि मथुरा में केवल बौद्ध
गांधार को केवल सातवाहनों ने संरक्षण दिया
मथुरा बुद्ध में लहरदार यूनानी केश हैं
e: Gandhara art (NW frontier—Taxila, Peshawar) blended Buddhist themes with Greco-Roman techniques (Apollo-like features, wavy hair, heavy drapery, grey/blue schist/stucco). Mathura art (indigenous) used spotted red sandstone (Sikri) and depicted Buddhist, Jain, and Brahmanical deities (plus headless statue of Kanishka).
qe: Which of the following features distinguishes the "Gandhara School of Art" from the "Mathura School of Art" during the Kushana period?
oe: Gandhara used grey/bluish schist stone with Greco-Roman realism, while Mathura used spotted red sandstone with indigenous spiritual symbolism
Gandhara produced images of Jain, Hindu, and Buddhist deities, while Mathura produced only Buddhist images
Gandhara art was patronized solely by Satavahanas, while Mathura was patronized by Guptas
Mathura Buddha has wavy Greek hair and Apollo-like muscles, whereas Gandhara Buddha is clean-shaven

q: 57 ई.पू. से प्रारंभ होने वाला "विक्रम संवत्" प्रारंभिक अभिलेखों में विक्रमादित्य से जुड़ने से पूर्व किस प्राचीन भारतीय गणराज्य / वंश से संबद्ध था?
e: The 57 BCE era originally appeared in inscriptions as the "Krita Era" and "Malava Era" (used by the Malava republic of Rajasthan/Malwa) commemorating the expulsion of Shakas from Ujjain in 57 BCE, later styled the Vikrama Samvat.
qe: The "Vikrama Era" (विक्रम संवत्, beginning in 57 BCE) is historically linked in early inscriptions with which ancient Indian tribal republic / dynasty before being associated with Vikramaditya?

q: प्रसिद्ध पालि बौद्ध ग्रंथ "मिलिंदपन्हो" (मिलिंद के प्रश्न) में हिंद-यवन शासक मिनांडर प्रथम और किस बौद्ध भिक्षु के बीच दार्शनिक संवाद संकलित है?
e: Milindapanho records the dialogue between Indo-Greek ruler Menander I (capital Sakala/Sialkot, 165–130 BCE) and Buddhist sage Nagasena, resulting in Menander's conversion to Buddhism. Exam Boosters: (1) Indo-Greeks were the FIRST rulers in India to issue portrait coins with king's name/title and the first to issue gold coins in India.
qe: The famous Pali Buddhist text "Milindapanho" (Questions of Milinda) records the philosophical dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander I and which Buddhist monk?

q: प्राकृत भाषा एवं ब्राह्मी लिपि में लिखा गया हाथीगुम्फा अभिलेख (उदयगिरि पहाड़ी, ओडिशा) कलिंग के किस चेदि (महामेघवाहन) शासक का प्रमुख जीवनी-स्रोत है?
e: King Kharavela (1st century BCE, devout follower of Jainism) issued the 17-line Hathigumpha inscription detailing 13 years of his reign, including extending a canal originally excavated by a Nanda king and defeating Magadha. Exam Boosters: (1) Gondophernes was the famous Indo-Parthian (Pahlava) king during whose reign St. Thomas is traditionally believed to have visited India.
qe: The Hathigumpha Inscription (Udayagiri Hills, Odisha), written in Prakrit language and Brahmi script, is the primary biographical source for which Chedi (Mahameghavahana) ruler of Kalinga?

q: प्रथम शताब्दी ई. की किस अज्ञात यूनानी समुद्री पुस्तिका में भारत-रोम समुद्री व्यापार, मानसून पवनों (हिप्पालस द्वारा खोजी गई) तथा भड़ौच (बैरीगाज़ा), मुज़िरिस व अरिकामेडु बंदरगाहों का सजीव वर्णन है?
e: "Periplus of the Erythraean Sea" (c. 1st century CE) is the premier eyewitness account of Indo-Roman trade. Exam Boosters: (1) Pliny the Elder's "Naturalis Historia" (77 CE) lamented the drain of Roman gold coins into India for luxury goods (spices, muslin, ivory, gems). (2) Arikamedu (Puducherry) yielded Roman amphorae and Arretine pottery.
qe: Which anonymous 1st-century CE Greek maritime handbook vividly describes Indo-Roman sea trade, monsoon winds (discovered by Hippalus), and Indian ports like Barygaza (Bharuch), Muziris, and Arikamedu?

q:
सातवाहन प्रशासनिक व सामाजिक व्यवस्था के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: सातवाहन राजा प्रायः मातृनाम (जैसे गौतमीपुत्र, वासिष्ठीपुत्र) का प्रयोग करते थे, फिर भी राजसिंहासन का उत्तराधिकार पूर्णतः पितृसत्तात्मक था।
कथन II: "आहार" नामक प्रशासनिक इकाइयों के प्रमुख "अमात्य" होते थे, जबकि ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में स्थित सैन्य शिविर "कटक" व "स्कंधावार" कहलाते थे।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: न तो I और न ही II
e: Both statements are historically accurate. Satavahanas practiced matronymic naming while maintaining patrilineal succession; their districts were called Aharas (under Amatyas), rural headmen were Gaulmikas, and military camps were Katakas/Skandhavaras.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the Satavahana administrative and social system:
Statement I: Satavahana kings frequently used matronymics (names derived from their mothers, e.g., Gautamiputra, Vasishthiputra), yet royal succession remained strictly patrilineal.
Statement II: Rural administrative units called "Ahara" were headed by "Amatyas", while military regiments stationed in rural areas were called "Kataka" and "Skandhavara".
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: कौन-सा गुप्त शासक "महाराजाधिराज" की भव्य शाही उपाधि धारण करने तथा 319–320 ई. में गुप्त संवत् प्रारंभ करने वाला प्रथम शासक था?
e: Chandragupta I (319–335 CE) married Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi (commemorated on gold coins), assumed the title Maharajadhiraja, and founded the Gupta Era (319–320 CE). Exam Boosters: (1) Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha held only the modest title "Maharaja".
qe: Which Gupta ruler was the first to assume the grand imperial title "Maharajadhiraja" and initiate the Gupta Era in 319–320 CE?

q: समुद्रगुप्त की सैन्य विजयों की प्रशंसा करने वाली प्रसिद्ध "प्रयाग प्रशस्ति" (इलाहाबाद स्तंभ लेख) की रचना संस्कृत चम्पू शैली (गद्य + पद्य) में किसने की थी?
e: Harishena (Samudragupta's Sandhivigrahika — Minister of Peace & War, Kumaramatya, and Mahadandanayaka) composed the 33-line Prayag Prashasti. Exam Boosters: (1) Samudragupta followed "Prasabhodharana" (total annexation) in Aryavarta (North India) and "Grahana-Moksha-Anugraha" (capture, release, reinstate) in Dakshinapatha (12 southern kings). (2) He is depicted playing the Veena on his gold coins ("Kaviraja").
qe: Who composed the famous "Prayag Prashasti" (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) in Sanskrit Champu style (prose + verse), eulogizing the military conquests of Samudragupta?

q: किस गुप्त शासक के शासनकाल में चीनी बौद्ध यात्री फाह्यान (399–414 ई.) भारत आया और उसने "फो-क्यो-की" नामक यात्रावृत्तांत लिखा?
e: Fa-Hien visited India during Chandragupta II's reign (though he never mentioned the emperor's name), praising the mild criminal justice, absence of capital punishment, vegetarianism, charitable hospitals, and use of cowrie shells (कौड़ियाँ) for everyday transactions.
qe: During whose reign did the Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa-Hien (Faxian) visit India (399–414 CE) and write "Fo-Kuo-Ki"?

q: किस गुप्त सम्राट ने मध्य एशियाई आक्रमणकारी हूणों को पराजित किया था, जिसका उल्लेख गाजीपुर (उ.प्र.) स्थित भीतरी स्तंभ लेख में मिलता है?
e: Skandagupta (455–467 CE, title "Kramaditya") decisively repulsed the Huna invasion (recorded in the Bhitari Pillar Inscription, Ghazipur, UP and Junagadh Rock Inscription, where his governor Parnadatta/Chakrapalita again repaired Sudarshana Lake). Exam Boosters: (1) Kumaragupta I (415–455 CE, title Mahendraditya) founded Nalanda Mahavihara and issued the largest variety of Gupta coins.
qe: Which Gupta emperor defeated the fierce Central Asian invaders, the Hunas (led by Khushnawaz / Toramana precursors), as recorded in the Bhitari Pillar Inscription (Ghazipur, UP)?

q: देवगढ़ (ललितपुर, उ.प्र.) स्थित प्रसिद्ध "दशावतार मंदिर"—शिखर और पंचायतन शैली के प्रारंभिक पाषाण मंदिरों में से एक—किस काल से संबंधित है?
e: The Dashavatara Temple (Deogarh, Lalitpur, UP; dedicated to Vishnu, famous for Sheshashayi Vishnu panel) is the masterpiece of Gupta Nagara temple architecture. Exam Boosters: (1) Other famous Gupta temples: Bhitargaon Brick Temple (Kanpur Dehat, UP), Parvati Temple (Nachna Kuthara, MP), Shiva Temple (Bhumara, MP), Vishnu Temple (Tigawa, MP).
qe: The iconic "Dashavatara Temple" at Deogarh (Lalitpur, UP)—one of the earliest surviving Panchayatan-style stone temples with a Shikhara—belongs to which period?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन उज्जैन में चंद्रगुप्त द्वितीय विक्रमादित्य के दरबार के "नवरत्नों" में सम्मिलित नहीं था?
e: Aryabhata (born 476 CE, Kusumapura/Patna; authored Aryabhatiya & Surya Siddhanta) lived after Chandragupta II (375–415 CE), and Banabhatta was Harshavardhana's court poet (7th century). The 9 Navaratnas were Kalidasa, Dhanvantari, Kshapanaka, Amarasimha (Amarkosha), Shanku, Vetalabhatta, Ghatakarpara, Varahamihira (Brihatsamhita), and Vararuchi.
qe: Who among the following was NOT one of the "Navaratnas" (Nine Gems) at the court of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya in Ujjain?

q: गुप्त सम्राटों द्वारा जारी किए गए स्वर्ण सिक्कों तथा चाँदी के सिक्कों को आधिकारिक रूप से क्रमशः क्या कहा जाता था?
e: Gupta gold coins were called "Dinara" (दीनार — largest number of gold coins in ancient India), and silver coins (first issued by Chandragupta II after defeating Shaka ruler Rudrasimha III of Western India) were called "Rupaka" (रूपक).
qe: What were the gold coins and silver coins issued by the Gupta emperors officially called respectively?

q: भारत में "सती प्रथा" का प्राचीनतम अभिलेखीय साक्ष्य (510 ई., गोपराज की पत्नी के सती होने का उल्लेख) किस स्थान से प्राप्त हुआ है?
e: The Eran Pillar Inscription (510 CE, Sagar district, MP) of Gupta king Bhanugupta records the death of his general Gopraja in battle against the Hunas and his wife committing Sati—the first epigraphic evidence of Sati. Exam Boosters: (1) Mehrauli Iron Pillar (Delhi, rust-free iron) mentions King "Chandra" (identified with Chandragupta II). (2) Mandasor Inscription (Vatsabhatti) describes a silk-weavers' guild (Shreni) during Kumaragupta I's reign.
qe: The earliest epigraphic (inscriptional) evidence of the practice of "Sati" in India (dated 510 CE, recording the self-immolation of Gopraja's wife) was discovered at:

q: गुप्तकालीन प्रशासनिक पदानुक्रम में प्रादेशिक इकाइयों को सबसे बड़े से सबसे छोटे के क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
e: Gupta Empire was divided into provinces called Bhukti/Desha (headed by Uparika), subdivided into districts called Vishaya (headed by Vishayapati), further into Vithi/Peth, and down to the village unit Grama (headed by Gramika).
qe: In the Gupta administrative hierarchy, arrange the territorial divisions from LARGEST to SMALLEST:

q: गुप्तकालीन कोश "अमरकोश" (अमरसिंह कृत) में परिभाषित निम्नलिखित भूमि प्रकारों में से कौन-सा सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
o: uncultivated land (खिल — बंजर / जोती न जाने वाली भूमि)
वास्तु — पशुओं के चरने योग्य चारागाह भूमि
e: In Amarkosha, "Vastu" meant habitable/residential land (वास योग्य भूमि), whereas pasture land was called "Gapata Saraha" (गोपत सराह / चारागाह). Kshetra, Khila, and Aprahata are correctly matched.
qe: Which of the following land types defined in the Gupta-period lexicon "Amarkosha" (by Amarasimha) is NOT correctly matched?

q: किस गुप्तकालीन खगोलविद् और गणितज्ञ ने "पंचसिद्धांतिका" तथा "बृहत्संहिता" की रचना की, जिसमें रोमक व पौलिश सहित पाँच खगोल प्रणालियों का समन्वय है?
e: Varahamihira (6th century CE, Ujjain) authored Panchasiddhantika, Brihatsamhita (encyclopaedia of astronomy, architecture, botany, meteorology), and Brihajjataka. Exam Boosters: (1) Brahmagupta (7th century, Bhinmal) authored Brahmasphutasiddhanta (rules for zero and negative numbers; anticipated gravity before Newton).
qe: Which Gupta-era astronomer and mathematician wrote "Panchasiddhantika" and "Brihatsamhita", synthesizing five astronomical systems including Romaka and Paulisha Siddhantas?

q:
गुप्तयुगीन अर्थव्यवस्था एवं समाज के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: गुप्तकाल में मध्य व पश्चिमी भारत में "विष्टि" (बेगार) को राजकीय आय का स्रोत माना जाता था और यह व्यापक रूप से प्रचलित थी।
कथन II: गुप्तकाल में शूद्रों की स्थिति में आंशिक सुधार हुआ (उन्हें रामायण-महाभारत-पुराण सुनने व कृषि की अनुमति मिली), जबकि फाह्यान ने चांडालों (अस्पृश्यों) पर कठोर प्रतिबंधों का उल्लेख किया।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: न तो I और न ही II
e: Both statements are completely accurate (classic NCERT/R. S. Sharma UP TGT facts). Also, the first clear emergence of the Kayastha scribe caste occurred during the Gupta period due to extensive land grant documentation.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gupta Age economy and society:
Statement I: Forced labour ("Vishti") was considered a source of state income and was widely prevalent in central and western India during the Gupta period.
Statement II: The position of Shudras improved slightly in the Gupta period as they were permitted to listen to the Epics and Puranas and practice agriculture, whereas untouchables (Chandalas) faced severe restrictions noted by Fa-Hien.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: महाराष्ट्र की अजंता गुफाओं में से कौन-सी गुफाएँ गुप्त-वाकाटक काल के भित्ति चित्रों (जातक कथाएँ, मरणासन्न राजकुमारी तथा बोधिसत्व पद्मपाणि) के लिए प्रसिद्ध हैं?
e: Out of 29 Buddhist caves at Ajanta, Caves 16 (Dying Princess), 17 (Mother & Child, Rahul Samarpan — "Chitrashala"), 1 (Padmapani & Vajrapani), and 2 belong to the Gupta-Vakataka golden era (5th–6th centuries CE).
qe: Which of the following caves at Ajanta (Maharashtra) are famous for Gupta-Vakataka period mural paintings depicting Jataka tales, the Dying Princess, and Bodhisattva Padmapani?

q: किस चीनी बौद्ध यात्री ने हर्षवर्धन (606–647 ई.) के शासनकाल में भारत की यात्रा की, आचार्य शीलभद्र के अधीन नालंदा विश्वविद्यालय में अध्ययन किया तथा "सी-यू-की" की रचना की?
e: Hiuen Tsang ("Prince of Pilgrims", 629–645 CE) presided over Harsha's Kannauj Religious Assembly (643 CE) and attended the quinquennial Prayag Assembly (Mahamokshaparishad). Exam Boosters: (1) Harsha authored three Sanskrit plays: Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, and Nagananda. (2) Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari.
qe: Which Chinese Buddhist traveller visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana (606–647 CE), studied at Nalanda University under Acharya Shilabhadra, and wrote "Si-Yu-Ki"?

q: जैन कवि रविकीर्ति द्वारा रचित प्रसिद्ध "एहोल अभिलेख" में नर्मदा नदी के तट पर हर्षवर्धन के विरुद्ध बादामी के किस चालुक्य शासक की निर्णायक विजय का उल्लेख है?
e: Pulakeshin II (610–642 CE) defeated Harshavardhana on the Narmada (c. 618 CE) and assumed the title "Parameshwara". Later, Pallava king Narasimhavarman I ("Vatapikonda") defeated and killed Pulakeshin II in 642 CE.
qe: The famous "Aihole Inscription" (composed by Jain poet Ravikirti) records the decisive victory of which Chalukya king of Badami over Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada River?

q: किस राष्ट्रकूट शासक ने महाराष्ट्र के एलोरा में भव्य एकाश्म शैलकृत "कैलाशनाथ मंदिर" (गुफा संख्या 16) का निर्माण करवाया था?
e: Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (756–774 CE) carved the Kailasanatha Temple at Ellora top-down from a single basalt rock. Exam Boosters: (1) Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty (capital Manyakheta). (2) Amoghavarsha I wrote "Kavirajamarga" (earliest Kannada poetics work).
qe: Which Rashtrakuta ruler commissioned the magnificent monolithic rock-cut "Kailasanatha Temple" (Cave 16) at Ellora, Maharashtra?

q: कन्नौज पर आधिपत्य के लिए प्रसिद्ध "त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष" (8वीं–10वीं शताब्दी ई.) किन तीन राजवंशों के बीच लड़ा गया था?
e: The Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj (symbol of North Indian imperial sovereignty after Harsha) involved the Palas (Bengal—Dharmapala), Gurjara-Pratiharas (Western India—Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mihira Bhoja), and Rashtrakutas (Deccan—Dhruva, Govinda III), with the Gurjara-Pratiharas ultimately retaining Kannauj.
qe: The famous "Tripartite Struggle" (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष, 8th–10th centuries CE) for supremacy over Kannauj was fought among which three dynasties?

q: पाल वंश के दौरान प्रसिद्ध "विक्रमशिला विश्वविद्यालय" (भागलपुर, बिहार) की स्थापना तथा नालंदा विश्वविद्यालय का पुनरुद्धार किसने किया था?
e: Pala ruler Dharmapala (770–810 CE) founded Vikramashila Mahavihara (premier centre of Vajrayana Buddhism) and Somapura Mahavihara (Paharpur). Exam Boosters: (1) Gopala (750 CE) founded the Pala dynasty (elected by regional chieftains to end Matsyanyaya/anarchy) and built Odantapuri University.
qe: Who founded the famous "Vikramashila University" (Bhagalpur, Bihar) and revived Nalanda University during the Pala Dynasty?

q: महाबलिपुरम (ममल्लापुरम, तमिलनाडु) का विश्वप्रसिद्ध "तट मंदिर" (Shore Temple) और एकाश्म "पंच रथ" (सप्त पैगोडा) किस दक्षिण भारतीय राजवंश द्वारा बनवाए गए थे?
e: The Pallavas of Kanchipuram pioneered Dravidian temple architecture: Narasimhavarman I ("Mamalla") built the rock-cut Pancha Rathas (Mamalla style), and Narasimhavarman II ("Rajasimha") built the structural Shore Temple and Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram.
qe: The world-famous "Shore Temple" and the monolithic "Pancha Rathas" (Seven Pagodas) at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram, Tamil Nadu) were built by which South Indian dynasty?

q: किस चोल सम्राट ने तंजावुर में भव्य "बृहदीश्वर (राजराजेश्वर) मंदिर" (1010 ई.) का निर्माण कराया तथा उत्तरी श्रीलंका व मालदीव पर विजय प्राप्त की?
e: Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE) built the granite Brihadeeswarar Temple (UNESCO site) and initiated Chola naval dominance. His son Rajendra I (1014–1044 CE) conquered all of Sri Lanka, marched to the Ganga ("Gangaikondachola"), built Gangaikonda Cholapuram, and led a naval expedition against the Srivijaya Empire (SE Asia).
qe: Which Chola emperor constructed the magnificent "Brihadeeswarar (Rajarajeshwara) Temple" at Thanjavur (1010 CE) and conquered northern Sri Lanka and the Maldives?

q: 'लुप्त मोम' विधि से निर्मित "नटराज" (तांडव मुद्रा में ब्रह्मांडीय नृत्य करते शिव) की प्रसिद्ध कांस्य मूर्ति किस राजवंश की मूर्तिकला का चरमोत्कर्ष है?
e: Chola bronze sculptures—above all the four-armed Nataraja—are world-renowned masterpieces of Indian metallurgy and iconography. Exam Boosters: (1) Under Chola local administration, "Ur" was the general village assembly, "Sabha/Mahasabha" was the Brahmana village (Agrahara) assembly, and "Nagaram" was the merchant town assembly.
qe: The famous bronze sculpture of "Nataraja" (Shiva as Lord of Cosmic Dance in Tandava pose), crafted by the lost-wax method, represents the zenith of sculptural art under which dynasty?

q: 712 ई. में रावर के युद्ध में राजा दाहिर को पराजित कर सिंध पर प्रथम सफल अरब मुस्लिम आक्रमण का नेतृत्व किसने किया था?
e: Umayyad general Muhammad bin Qasim (sent by Al-Hajjaj, Governor of Iraq) conquered Sindh and Multan in 712 CE (detailed in "Chachnama"), introducing Jizya tax in Sindh for the first time and facilitating the transmission of Indian astronomy (Brahmasphutasiddhanta) and numerals ("Hindsa") to the Arab world.
qe: In 712 CE, who led the first successful Arab Muslim conquest of Sindh, defeating Raja Dahir at the Battle of Rewar?

q: महमूद गजनवी के साथ भारत (1017–1030 ई.) आए किस प्रसिद्ध मध्य एशियाई विद्वान ने संस्कृत सीखी और 11वीं शताब्दी के भारतीय समाज व विज्ञान का वस्तुनिष्ठ ग्रंथ "किताब-उल-हिंद" (तहकीक-ए-हिंद) लिखा?
e: Abu Rayhan Al-Biruni (from Khwarizm) wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in Arabic (80 chapters) and was the first Muslim scholar to study the Puranas. Exam Boosters: (1) Mahmud of Ghazni raided India 17 times (1000–1027 CE), notably plundering Somnath Temple in 1025 CE (during Bhima I's reign). (2) Firdausi wrote "Shahnama" (Homer of the East); Utbi wrote "Kitab-ul-Yamini".
qe: Which celebrated Central Asian scholar accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni to India (1017–1030 CE), mastered Sanskrit, and authored "Kitab-ul-Hind" (Tahqiq-i-Hind), a remarkably objective account of 11th-century Indian society and science?

q:
उत्तर भारत में मुहम्मद गोरी के निम्नलिखित निर्णायक युद्धों को सही कालानुक्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
1. तराइन का प्रथम युद्ध
2. जयचंद के विरुद्ध चंदावर का युद्ध
3. तराइन का द्वितीय युद्ध
4. मूलराज द्वितीय / भीम द्वितीय के विरुद्ध कायादारा (गुजरात) युद्ध
e: Correct chronology: (4) Battle of Kayadara/Anhilwara (1178 CE — Ghori's first defeat in India by Queen Naikidevi & Bhima II/Mulraja II of Solanki Gujarat) → (1) 1st Battle of Tarain (1191 CE — Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Ghori) → (3) 2nd Battle of Tarain (1192 CE — Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, laying the foundation of Turkish rule) → (2) Battle of Chandawar (1194 CE — Ghori defeated Gahadavala king Jaichand of Kannauj).
qe:
Arrange the following decisive battles of Muhammad Ghori in North India in correct chronological order:
1. First Battle of Tarain (तराइन का प्रथम युद्ध)
2. Battle of Chandawar against Jaichand (चंदावर का युद्ध)
3. Second Battle of Tarain (तराइन का द्वितीय युद्ध)

q:
भारत पर प्रारंभिक तुर्की आक्रमणों (गजनवी और गोरी) के प्रभाव के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: जहाँ महमूद गजनवी के आक्रमण मुख्यतः धन लूटने व मध्य एशियाई साम्राज्य के वित्तपोषण हेतु थे, वहीं मुहम्मद गोरी का उद्देश्य भारत में स्थायी क्षेत्रीय राज्य की स्थापना था।
कथन II: गोरी के सेनापति बख्तियार खिलजी ने लगभग 1193–1203 ई. में नालंदा व विक्रमशिला विश्वविद्यालयों को नष्ट कर दिया, जिससे पूर्वी भारत में संस्थागत बौद्ध धर्म का पतन तीव्र हो गया।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: न तो I और न ही II
e: Both statements are historically accurate. Unlike Ghazni (who annexed only Punjab), Ghori left his slave-general Qutbuddin Aibak in charge of conquered Indian territories, leading directly to the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate in 1206 CE.
